verses.zh: （大卫的诗。）耶和华啊，求你为我伸冤，因我向来行事纯全；我又倚靠耶和华，并不摇动。
verses.en: By David.Vindicate me, O Lord,for I have integrity,[NOTE:1] and I trust in the Lord without wavering.
notes: Psalm 26. The author invites the Lord to test his integrity, asserts his innocence and declares his loyalty to God.
verses.commentary:
26:1-7 This strophe asserts the psalmist's desire to be vindicated by YHWH. He has been accused
of some evil, possibly idolatry.

- vindicate – BDB 1047, KB1022, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 7:8; 17:2-3;
35:24; 43:1; YHWH tests His people, cf. Jer. 11:20; 12:3; 20:12; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD
TESTS HIS PEOPLE at Ps. 11:4b

- examine me – BDB 103, KB 119, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 139:23

- test my mind – BDB 650, KB 707, Piel IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 7:9;
the mind (lit. "kidneys") and heart were idioms for the whole person (i.e., thoughts,
motives, actions; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: INWARD PARTS)

The author then lists the reasons why he should be vindicated.

- I have walked in my integrity – BDB 229, KB 246, Qal PERFECT,
cf. Ps. 26:3b and 26:11a; Job 4:6; Ps. 7:8; 25:21; 41:12; 78:72; 101:2; Prov. 2:7; 19:1;
20:7; 28:6

- I have trusted in YHWH without wavering – notice the two VERBS.

- trusted – BDB 105, KB 120, Qal PERFECT, cf. Ps. 13:5; 25:2;
52:8; this is a settled condition

- without wavering – BDB 588, KB 609, Qal IMPERFECT which
is an ongoing need (cf. Heb. 10:23); similar imagery occurs in Ps. 5:8 and 18:36

- I have walked in Your truth – BDB 229, KB 246, Hithpael PERFECT
with waw; truth (BDB 54) here means faithfulness, not creedal (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

- I do not sit with deceitful men – BDB 442, KB 444, Qal PERFECT,
cf. Ps. 1:1 (this may refer to idolatry, cf. NIDOTTE, vol. 4, p. 54)

- I do not go with pretenders – BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERFECT;
pretenders (BDB 761, KB 834, Niphal PARTICIPLE) denotes someone who
conceals things

- I hate the assembly of evil doers – BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal PERFECT,
cf. Ps. 31:6; 139:21

- I will not sit with the wicked – BDB 442, KB 444, Qal IMPERFECT

- I will wash my hands in innocence – BDB 934, KB 1220, Qal IMPERFECT,
cf. Ps. 73:13; Numbers 8 and 9 are ritual acts performed in national worship events (cf. Deut. 21:6)

- I will go about Your altar – BDB 685, KB 738, Poel COHORTATIVE, this refers
to some kind of ritual dance or march, cf. Josh. 6:3-15; Ps. 43:3-4; 48:12

- I will proclaim all Your wonders (see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: WONDERFUL THINGS)

- singing aloud – BDB 1033, KB 1570, Hiphil INFINITIVE
CONSTRUCT

- proclaim – BDB 707, KB 765, Piel INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT ,
cf. Ps. 9:1; 40:5; 75:1

Notice the variations between PERFECTS and IMPERFECTS. Remember,
time is not part of Hebrew VERBS, just completed or ongoing action.

▣ Notice how the opponents of faithful followers are characterized.

- deceitful men (i.e., idolators, worthless, BDB 996, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY,
VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS)

- pretenders (i.e., hypocrites, BDB 761, KB 824, Niphal PARTICIPLE)

- the assembly of evil doers (BDB 949, KB 1269, Hiphil PARTICIPLE)

- wicked (BDB 957)

Also, all the psalmist's positive actions could be understood as not performed
by his opponents. He is innocent and asks for vindication. They are guilty and deserve condemnation.

The list of descriptive terms for his opponents (cf. Ps. 1:5; 5:10; 15:2-5) is
expanded in the next strophe.

- sinners (BDB 308)

- men of bloodshed (BDB 60 CONSTRUCT BDB 196, cf. Ps. 5:6; 55:23; 139:19)

- wicked schemers (BDB 273, cf. Ps. 37:7), AB suggests this refers to idols (p. 163)

- offer bribes (BDB 1005), cf. Exod. 23:8; Deut. 16:19; Ps. 15:5

One wonders who these people are. Are they covenant people who live faithless lives or
non-covenant people with no light? God help us, they seem to be people who had light, truth, and
revelation but chose to reject it!

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你察看我，试验我，熬炼我的肺腑心肠。
verses.en: Examine me, O Lord, and test me.Evaluate my inner thoughts and motives.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for I in my integrity walk.”

verses.zh: 因为你的慈爱常在我眼前，我也按你的真理而行。
verses.en: For I am ever aware of your faithfulness,[NOTE:1] and your loyalty continually motivates me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “evaluate my kidneys and my heart.” The kidneys and heart were viewed as the seat of one’s volition, conscience, and moral character.
Heb “for your faithfulness [is] before my eyes.”

verses.zh: 我没有和虚谎人同坐，也不与瞒哄人的同群。
verses.en: I do not associate[NOTE:1] with deceitful men,or consort[NOTE:2] with those who are dishonest.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and I walk about in your loyalty.”sn The psalmist’s awareness of the Lord’s faithfulness and…loyalty toward him motivates him to remain loyal to the Lord and to maintain his moral purity.
Heb “sit.”
Heb “go.” The psalmist uses the imperfect form of the verb to emphasize that he does not make a practice of associating with such people.

verses.zh: 我恨恶恶人的会，必不与恶人同坐。
verses.en: I hate the mob[NOTE:1] of evil men,and do not associate[NOTE:2] with the wicked.
notes: Heb “[those who] conceal themselves.”
Heb “assembly, company.”
verses.commentary:
26:5 "the assembly of evildoers" The word "assembly" (qahal, BDB 874)
is the OT background to the NT designation of the church, ekklesia (lit. "the called out
ones," i.e., the church) used in the LXX to translate qahal.

The idea is that there are two kinds of assemblies (cf. Matt. 7:13-14)

- the faithful people of God – Ps. 22:22,25; 35:18; 40:9,10; 89:5; 107:32; 149:1

- the evildoers (i.e., idolaters, cf. Ps. 31:6)

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHURCH (ekklēsia)

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我要洗手表明无辜，才环绕你的祭坛；
verses.en: I maintain a pure lifestyle,[NOTE:1] so I can appear before your altar,[NOTE:2] O Lord,
notes: Heb “sit.” The psalmist uses the imperfect form of the verb to emphasize that he does not make a practice of associating with such people.
Heb “I wash my hands in innocence.” The psalmist uses an image from cultic ritual to picture his moral lifestyle. The imperfect verbal emphasizes that this is his habit.

verses.zh: 我好发称谢的声音，也要述说你一切奇妙的作为。
verses.en: to give you thanks,[NOTE:1] and to tell about all your amazing deeds.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “so I can go around your altar” (probably in ritual procession). Following the imperfect of the preceding line, the cohortative with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose or result.
Heb “to cause to be heard the sound of thanksgiving.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我喜爱你所住的殿和你显荣耀的居所。
verses.en: O Lord, I love the temple where you live,[NOTE:1] the place where your splendor is revealed.[NOTE:2]
notes: The two infinitival forms (both with prefixed preposition ל, lamed) give the purpose for his appearance at the altar.
Heb “the dwelling of your house.”
verses.commentary:
26:8-12 This strophe parallels the thoughts of Ps. 26:1-7. The psalmist again lists his
qualification for acceptance and his opponents' actions/motives for rejection.

The psalmist's qualifications:

- I love the temple ‒ BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PERFECT

- I walk in integrity — BDB 1070, cf. Ps. 26:1

- my foot stands on a level place (cf. Ps. 5:8; 27:11). This is imagery for the clear path,
the level way of YHWH's covenant, cf. Ps. 119:105 (see

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

The psalmist asks God to act toward him differently than the way He acts toward the
wicked.

- Do not take my soul away along with sinners (i.e., "gather," BDB 62, KB 74,
Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense. This
VERB is used literally of "harvest" (cf. Isa. 62:9). It came to
be used of death (cf. Jdgs. 2:10; 2 Kgs. 22:20; 2 Chr. 34:28).

- Do not take my life with men of bloodshed

These people are characterized by bloodshed, wicked schemes, and bribery. There is a
clear obvious lifestyle difference between the faithful follower and the faithless Israelite who
performs the acts of worship and participates in the ritual but there is no lifestyle effect
(cf. Matt. 7:15-27)!

SPECIAL
TOPIC: APOSTASY (APHISTĒMI)

26:8 This imagery refers to the tabernacle of the wilderness (cf. Exodus 25-31, 36-40), but
later came to refer to the temple in Jerusalem on Mt. Moriah. It was where YHWH dwelt among humans
(i.e., between the wings of the Cherubim above the ark of the covenant in the Holy of Holies).
Faithful followers longed to be in YHWH's presence (cf. Ps. 23:6; 27:4-5).

Psalm 26:6 also refers to the tabernacle/temple (cf. Ps. 24:3-4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ARK OF THE COVENANT

verses.zh: 不要把我的灵魂和罪人一同除掉；不要把我的性命和流人血的一同除掉。
verses.en: Do not sweep me away[NOTE:1] with sinners,or execute me along with violent people,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the place of the abode of your splendor.”
Heb “do not gather up my life with.”

verses.zh: 他们的手中有奸恶，右手满有贿赂。
verses.en: who are always ready to do wrong[NOTE:1] or offer a bribe.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “or with men of bloodshed my life.” The verb is supplied; it is understood by ellipsis (see the preceding line).
Heb “who [have] in their hands evil.”

verses.zh: 至于我，却要行事纯全；求你救赎我，怜恤我！
verses.en: But I have integrity.[NOTE:1] Rescue me[NOTE:2] and have mercy on me!
notes: Heb “and their right hand is full of a bribe.”

Heb “and I in my integrity walk.” The psalmist uses the imperfect verbal form to emphasize this is his practice. The construction at the beginning of the verse (conjunction + pronoun) highlights the contrast between the psalmist and the sinners mentioned in vv. 9-10.
verses.commentary:
26:11 Even though the psalmist believes he is innocent, he knows that YHWH is pure and holy
and all humans are not (cf. Isa. 53:6; Rom. 1:18-3:18). The closer one comes into YHWH's fellowship
the more the awareness of personal sin (i.e., omission and commission) becomes a reality. Psalm 19:11-14
expresses this truth well.

26:11b Because of these things he asks YHWH to

- redeem him – BDB 804, KB 911, Qal IMPERATIVE, see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM

- be gracious to him – BDB 335, KB 334, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Ps. 25:16

He believes YHWH will vindicate him so he will bless YHWH

- with songs, Ps. 26:7

- with testimony, 26:7

- with blessing, 26:12 (BDB 138, KB 159, Piel IMPERFECT see
SPECIAL
TOPIC: Blessed [OT])

verses.zh: 我的脚站在平坦地方；在众会中我要称颂耶和华！
verses.en: I am safe,[NOTE:1] and among the worshipers I will praise the Lord.
notes: Or “redeem me.”
verses.commentary:
26:12 "My foot stands on a level place" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PATH, THE WAY

▣ "congregations" The MT is PLURAL but it may be an example of the
PLURAL OF MAJESTY. The NRSV, TEV, REB have the SINGULAR. The NET Bible
makes the PLURAL refer to the "worshipers" (cf. Knox Translation). The
PLURAL form appears only here and Ps. 68:26.

▣ "I shall bless the Lord" This refers to public
affirmation of one's faith, trust, hope, and allegiance to YHWH (cf. Rom. 10:9-13), probably in a
worship setting.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How does YHWH test the mind and heart?

- Does Ps. 26:6 imply a priest is the author?

- Define the word "wonders" (Ps. 26:7).

- Explain Ps. 26:12a in your own words.

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This Psalm, like much of Wisdom Literature, is based on the OT concept known as "the
two ways" (cf. Deut. 30:15,19; Psalm 1). There is prosperity for those who obey YHWH's
word and condemnation for those who do not (i.e., the cursings and blessings of Leviticus 26
and Deuteronomy 27-29).

- The psalmist apparently has been accused of some covenant violation. The best guess is idolatry.

- Psalm 26:9 implies an end-of-life separation between the faithful and unfaithful. The afterlife
in the OT is a vague (cf. Job 14:7-12,13-14; 19:25-27; Ps. 16:10; 49:15; 73:24; Isa. 25:8; 26:19;
Dan. 12:1-4) concept but progressive revelation (i.e., NT) clarifies the issue (cf. Matt. 25:46;
John 5:29; Acts 24:15; 1 Corinthians 15).
